description: Square pebble-wash terrazzo table slab on a single tapered cast concrete pedestal

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square pebble-wash terrazzo table, thick cast slab top with a chamfered edge, single tapered square concrete pedestal, square footing pad at the base Materials: pebble-wash terrazzo with exposed brown and white aggregate, algae staining in the low corners, chipped edges, water-darkened concrete pedestal.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90. 108/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two canvases, factory in 130 ms.

featureReviews.evidence: Built 0.620 x 0.720 x 0.620 m against the corrected declaration of 0.62 x 0.72 x 0.62 (plan corrected from 0.70 on the proxy's w/h = d/h = 0.860). Slab, sub-plate, post, footing, chamfer and pads all at the proxy band table's stations in fractions of H.
featureReviews.notes: Turntable silhouette identical at 0/90/180/270 by construction: four-fold plan symmetry.

featureReviews.evidence: 0.050 terrazzo slab on a 0.015 concrete sub-plate at 0.95 of its plan. Aggregate as a 512 px pebble canvas at 0.35 m: 2600 stones of 4-16 px in seven measured tones over a buff ground; probed on beauty-000 the top lands at luma 172 against the plate's 175 after two re-basings (197 -> 156 -> 172).
featureReviews.notes: First tile at 1500 stones to 30 px read as marbles; the plate's stones are 5-10 px on an 830 px slab.

featureReviews.evidence: 0.23 m square post, 0.365 m footing with a 23 mm chamfered cap stepping in to 0.86 of its plan, four 0.11 m corner pads under a notched base. One concrete tone (footing front renders 163 against the plate's 158) with a y tint to 0.78 under the slab standing in for the cast shadow the plate shows and the harness cannot.
featureReviews.notes: check-coplanar clean; the chamfer frustum starts inside the block at 2 mm less than its plan so no bbox face pairs.

name: Terrazzo Pedestal Park Table
nameTh: โต๊ะหินขัด
notes: The fixed public table found in Thai parks, school yards and temple grounds; heavy cast concrete, so it never moves and never folds. Empty top: nothing on it. Three chunky closed volumes -- slab, pedestal, footing -- which is the cheapest silhouette in this batch and the right one for a prop scattered across open ground. Shares its aggregate finish with the existing Pebble-Wash Terrazzo Paving Tile. Declared 0.70 x 0.72 x 0.70 m, inside the street-furniture prior of 0.3-1.8 m. PLAN CORRECTED FROM THE PROXY BEFORE BUILDING (2026-08-31): the list-time 0.70 x 0.72 x 0.70 has w/h 0.972, but the Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox w/h = d/h = 0.860 with a square plan. Height is the trustworthy axis for a table (a park table sits at dining height), so plan = 0.72 x 0.860 = 0.619 -> 0.62 m on both axes. Stack read off the proxy in fractions of H: slab 0.09 (a 0.050 terrazzo slab on a 0.015 concrete sub-plate at 0.95 W), pedestal 0.14-0.89 at 0.375 W = 0.23 m square, footing 0.02-0.13 at 0.59 W = 0.365 m square with a chamfered top and a notched base -- corner pads.
